title: Pricing the Repeat Repair Estimate — Service Accounts and Repair Orders
content:
## The two repairs
On a Service Accounts and Repair Orders account, the line estimated is the line of the latest diagnostic fee charged on the account, its posted labor rate is the one on that diagnostic fee, and its vehicle and odometer are those on that fee. The earlier repair is the repair order and concern line of the latest customer-pay parts charge recorded on the same vehicle, with every customer-pay parts and labor charge on that line. Wherever a record is chosen as the latest of its kind and two such records share that date, the one listed first in the records counts.

## When nothing is priced
- Where the account carries no diagnostic fee, or the vehicle on it has no earlier customer-pay parts charge, there is no repeat repair for this policy to price and it prices nothing.
- Where the diagnosis date is on or before the day the tier's repair warranty months (calendar months) after the earlier repair's line date (that month's last day where it has no such day) and the vehicle's odometer on the diagnostic fee is no more than the tier's repair warranty miles beyond the earlier repair's odometer, the failure is a comeback inside the store's repair warranty, its replacement parts are not billed and this policy prices nothing.
- Where the earlier repair's line carries no customer-pay labor charge, it is a parts sale rather than a repair the store performed, the failure does not repeat a repair, and this policy prices nothing.

The diagnosis date is the line date of the diagnostic fee; the earlier repair's odometer is the one recorded at check-in on its latest customer-pay parts charge.

## The estimate
The estimate is the labor amount plus the parts amount, rounded half up to the cent. The labor amount is the repair hours times the labor rate, less the tier's labor discount share of that product, the discount never more than the tier's largest labor discount per repair order. The repair hours are the hours of the earlier repair's latest customer-pay labor charge. The labor rate is the posted labor rate on the diagnostic fee. The parts amount is the total list price of the earlier repair's customer-pay parts charges less the tier's parts discount share.

## Order
The estimate is figured in this order: first the repair hours are multiplied by the labor rate and the tier discount, within its cap, is taken off; then every allowance this policy sets out is applied to that labor amount; then every index this policy sets out is applied to the earlier parts list price, and the indexed price is reduced once by the tier's parts discount and every further parts discount this policy sets out, added into one rate; and the labor and parts amounts are added and rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

## Worked figure (hypothetical: 10% labor discount capped at 100.00, 5% parts discount)
Earlier repair's latest labor charge 3.2 hours; posted rate on the diagnostic fee 140.00; earlier parts list price 268.00. Labor 448.00 less 44.80 is 403.20; parts 268.00 less 13.40 is 254.60; estimate 657.80.
